title: Sheafification preserves sections on a weakly contractible object
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $U$ be an affine object that is weakly contractible, meaning that every epimorphism of sheaves of sets on this site is surjective on sections over $U$. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets, abelian groups, or commutative rings on profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings. Form the presheaf $P_F$ by left Kan extension along $a_X^{op}$, where $a_X(S)=X[S]$ is the inverse limit of the finite disjoint unions of copies of $X$ indexed by finite continuous quotients of $S$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-point-lan-affine-evaluation]. Then the canonical sheafification map [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] $P_F(U)\to P_F^\#(U)$ is an isomorphism. This is natural in $F$ and in morphisms between weakly contractible affine objects and preserves addition and multiplication when present.

proof.text: Given a covering sieve S of the affine U, extract a pro-etale precoverage family and apply Mathlib QuasiCompactCover.exists_hom to obtain a finite affine refinement. For each affine Spec A in that refinement, apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-contractible-extension-full-site] to replace it by a singleton pro-etale affine cover Spec D -> Spec A, weakly contractible on the full small site of X. Compose these covers. The resulting finite family W_i -> U lies in S, covers U, and every W_i is affine and weakly contractible. Reindex the finite family by ULift (Fin (Nat.card I)) in Type u; surjective reindexing leaves the generated sieve unchanged. The argument includes the empty family.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-coproduct-evaluation] to W_i. It gives a coproduct V in the site (by reflection of colimits along the fully faithful universe-lifted Yoneda functor), the represented-sheaf coproduct, and the restriction-product bijection for every set sheaf on V. Let p:V -> U be the coproduct of the covering arrows. The map h_V -> h_U is epi: maps h_U -> H agreeing after p correspond to sections agreeing on the covering W_i -> U, hence are equal by sheaf separatedness and Yoneda. Apply the given weak contractibility of U to this epi and the identity section of h_U(U). The resulting actual site morphism sigma:U -> V satisfies sigma p=id_U. No clopen inheritance lemma is used.

For a Kan presheaf P, the last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-point-lan-affine-evaluation] makes its restriction fan over the finite weakly contractible affine W_i a limit fan at some coproduct. Transfer it to the chosen V using uniqueness of coproducts. The forgetful functor of each coefficient category preserves finite limits, so the underlying restriction map is bijective. Mathlib Sites.LocallyBijective gives covering equalizer and image sieves for the sheafification unit. For injectivity, refine the equalizer sieve as above, use injectivity of the restriction map on P(V), then pull back along sigma. For surjectivity, refine the image sieve, choose local representatives in P(W_i), combine them into s in P(V), and use the set-sheaf restriction bijection and unit naturality to show eta_V(s)=p^*t. Then sigma^*s maps to t because sigma p=id_U.

The preceding argument is written once for a concrete coefficient category whose forgetful functor preserves finite limits and reflects isomorphisms, and whose sheafification unit is locally bijective. Mathlib supplies these instances for Type (u+1), AddCommGrpCat and CommRingCat. The unit is already a morphism in the coefficient category, so its underlying bijectivity gives an isomorphism preserving all operations without constructing a separate algebra sheafification. The two naturality equations are respectively naturality of toSheafify as a presheaf morphism and the component of toSheafify_naturality for beta. Instantiate the generic proof with the three clauses of point_lan_affine_evaluation.
